chisel.builders_handbook.all_guides.desc: Have a browse and find your next building idea.
chisel.builders_handbook.empty: No guides here yet. Your next building adventure is still getting its pages together!
chisel.builders_handbook.intro: Got a pile of blocks and a big idea? Let's build something! Meet Chisel's tools, try a new palette and pick up a few tricks for making your next place feel like home.
chisel.builders_handbook.title:
Builder's 
Handbook
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.chec: Walk past your window as well as looking straight at it. If it looks good from both directions and nothing sticks into your path, you've found a keeper.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.comp: Left to right: flat glass, glass moved one block back, then the same recess with a frame in front. Spin them around and peek from the side. The wall stays put, so it's easier to spot what each change does.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.desc: A block forward or back can give a plain window a whole new look.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.edge: Roofs can play this game too. An overhang sticks out past the wall and gives the roof a clear edge. Try a short strip before doing the whole building, and leave room for doors, paths and neighbors.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.fram: The right window keeps that recess and adds a spruce ring one block in front of the wall. Now the window gets a little spotlight. The close-up below shows the same setup; turn it sideways to see the three layers.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.goal: Let's see what happens when a window stops sitting flush with the wall.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.plan: Picture the front of a wall as a flat sheet. Put something behind it and you've made a recess; bring something forward and it sticks out. Our little sample is five blocks wide and five tall, with a window one block wide and two tall.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.prac: Build the flat window and move its glass back one block. Take a look, then put it back. Try again with a frame around the recess. A few blocks and a pickaxe are all you need to audition the options.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.rece: The middle window only moves those two glass blocks back. From an angle, you can now see the edges of the opening. A tiny change makes the wall feel thicker.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.rest: You can stop at flat! A smooth modern wall might look great that way. Keep the extra depth where you like what it does. For actual shadows, have a look at the build in your world.
chisel.guide.adding_shape_and_depth.tran: Try a simple recess on a modern studio, or a chunky lintel over a shed door. Leave some flat wall around it so your favorite bit has room to stand out. Up next: Using Texture Intentionally.
chisel.guide.antiblock.description: Play with bold color and give your next room a look all its own.
chisel.guide.antiblock.title: Antiblock
chisel.guide.auto_chisel.description: Give your chiseling arm a break. This machine takes the next shift.
chisel.guide.auto_chisel.details: Put the variant you want in the center template slot. The machine chisels matching input blocks into that look and sends the results to the right. A fresh batch of fancy blocks, coming up!
chisel.guide.auto_chisel.tip: Planning a bigger project? Stack, Speed, Automation and Reversion Upgrades give this little workshop more ways to help.
chisel.guide.auto_chisel.title: Auto Chisel
chisel.guide.auto_chisel.usage: Right click to open the Auto Chisel. Give it a Chisel in the tool slot and feed your building blocks into the input above.
chisel.guide.auto_chisel_upgrades.descri: Help your Auto Chisel keep up with those castle-sized plans.
chisel.guide.auto_chisel_upgrades.detail: Ready for a production line? Automation enables external insertion into input slots and extraction from output slots. Reversion can work without a template, which is handy when your spare blocks need a fresh start.
chisel.guide.auto_chisel_upgrades.tip: Every upgrade has a home: pop it into the matching upgrade slot in the Auto Chisel.
chisel.guide.auto_chisel_upgrades.title: Auto Chisel Upgrades
chisel.guide.auto_chisel_upgrades.usage: Stack processes a full stack per cycle, and Speed shortens the wait. Automation lets other inventories feed the machine and collect its output. Reversion takes blocks back to their family's first variant.
chisel.guide.ball_o_moss.description: Instant 'this ruin has been here for ages' energy.
chisel.guide.ball_o_moss.details: The moss spreads unevenly, giving nearby surfaces a patchy, overgrown look. Lovely for old ruins or that corner the gardener keeps forgetting.
chisel.guide.ball_o_moss.tip: Each throw uses one Ball O' Moss. Try a small patch first to see how much wilderness your wall wants.
chisel.guide.ball_o_moss.title: Ball O' Moss
chisel.guide.ball_o_moss.usage: Right click to throw a Ball O' Moss. When it hits a block, it adds a moss overlay to nearby full blocks. Your garden wall just got a little more garden.
chisel.guide.builders_guide.description: Big dome dreams? Sketch the shape before hauling all those blocks.
chisel.guide.builders_guide.details: With an empty hand, right click the north or south face to adjust length, east or west for width, and top or bottom for height. Once the outline looks right, right click with a block to place material into the preview.
chisel.guide.builders_guide.tip: Can't see your outline clearly? Right click with dye to change its color. Set the shape and size before filling your masterpiece.
chisel.guide.builders_guide.title: Builder's Guide
chisel.guide.builders_guide.usage: Place the Builder's Guide. With an empty hand, sneak and right click to cycle through cuboids, spheres, domes and cylinders. Pick a shape that suits your grand plan.
chisel.guide.builders_handbook.descripti: A pocketful of ideas for the moment you stare at a wall and think, 'Now what?'
chisel.guide.builders_handbook.details: Use the arrows to turn pages or browse more entries. All Guides gathers every available guide, even ones without a category. Mark a favorite page with the bookmark so it's easy to come back.
chisel.guide.builders_handbook.tip: There's room for more inspiration: servers and data packs can add their own categories and guides.
chisel.guide.builders_handbook.title: Builder's Handbook
chisel.guide.builders_handbook.usage: Right click with the Builder's Handbook, then click the cover to open the table of contents. Pick a category and follow whichever idea catches your eye.
chisel.guide.chisel_concrete.description: From fresh city streets to well-traveled roads, give your town somewhere to go.
chisel.guide.chisel_concrete.title: Chisel Concrete / Asphalt
chisel.guide.chisel_concrete.usage: Pop gravel in a furnace to make Chisel Concrete, then use a Chisel to pick asphalt, concrete blocks or a weathered finish. Your next street is one batch away.
chisel.guide.chisels.description: One trusty tool, a whole new wardrobe for your blocks.
chisel.guide.chisels.details: Want to work on the wall itself? Left click a supported block to chisel it in place. Leave a chosen block in the Chisel slot to use that variant. Hold Shift and the Select Mode / Palette key, then release to confirm your mode.
chisel.guide.chisels.tip: Even trusty tools get tired: chiseling uses durability unless the server config disables it. Keep an eye on your Chisel while decorating.
chisel.guide.chisels.title: Chisels
chisel.guide.chisels.usage: Right click with a Chisel to open it. Pop a supported block in the Chisel slot and pick a decorative variant. Shift-click to give multiple stacks the same makeover.
chisel.guide.cloud.description: Put a little fluff in your skyline. Floating daydreams start here.
chisel.guide.cloud.title: Cloud
chisel.guide.cloud.usage: Throw a Cloud in a Bottle at a block to puff nearby air into cloud blocks. Then grab a Chisel and pick a decorative variant for your own little piece of sky.
chisel.guide.cloud_in_a_bottle.descripti: A little weather in your pocket. Forecast: fluffy.
chisel.guide.cloud_in_a_bottle.details: Each cloud takes a random shape around the impact point. Give it plenty of open air to puff out into, then see what the sky has cooked up.
chisel.guide.cloud_in_a_bottle.tip: Each throw uses one bottle. Aim where you want the cloud to gather, and leave room for a little surprise.
chisel.guide.cloud_in_a_bottle.title: Cloud in a Bottle
chisel.guide.cloud_in_a_bottle.usage: Right click to throw a Cloud in a Bottle at a block. On impact, nearby air fills with Cloud Blocks. An airy decoration, delivered with a splash.
chisel.guide.default_palette.usage: Fancy this mix? It's already waiting in your palette library. Select it with a Trowel and get building, or open it with the Palette Brush to swap materials and make it your own.
chisel.guide.default_palette.wall_tip: Take this sample wall for a spin! Drag to rotate, Shift-drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and double-click to reset. It shows the material proportions; your Trowel rolls a fresh mix from the materials you have available.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.check: A door you can spot, a path you can walk and light where you need it: that's a welcoming little build. If a decoration gets in the way, give it a better home.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.compar: The entrance on the left has a barrel in the way, two lanterns and a shiny gold strip above the frame. The right clears out the barrel, extra lantern and strip. Same doorway, less fuss. Which one would you rather come home to with a full inventory?
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.descri: A welcoming door, a useful lantern and somewhere to put all that stuff.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.focus: Where do you want someone to look first? On our workshop, it's the entrance. A frame and a nearby lantern give it some attention. Let the rest of the wall relax a little so the door stays easy to spot.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.goal: Time for the finishing touches. Let's make the entrance easy to find and easy to get through.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.lighti: Pick a fixture that feels at home: a lantern by the wooden workshop, or a simple lamp arrangement for a studio or shed. Place it where the light will help you find the door, use the workbench or follow a path.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.motif: Here's the quieter doorway up close: one spruce frame and a lantern beside it. A little matching spruce around selected windows can tie the build together. Put storage where it's handy, with enough room to walk past it. The barrel doesn't need to guard the door.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.night: Come back after sunset and look from the same spot. Can you find the door and see your way inside? Move a fixture if the useful bit is still dark. Start with the ordinary game view, then enjoy any shader extras you like.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.practi: Add something useful, like storage by the workbench, and a light that fits the building. Then try removing one decoration. Sometimes the finishing touch is picking a block back up. Take a daytime and nighttime wander through the result.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.previe: These previews keep everything bright so you can see the blocks. Check nighttime lighting in your world: a glowing texture may not cast light, and shaders can change the look.
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.title: Details and Lighting
chisel.guide.details_and_lighting.transf: Give a modern studio a simple frame and compact fixture, or repeat a sturdy support detail on a shed. You can leave a few walls quiet. Up next: Your First Build.
chisel.guide.energized_voidstone.descrip: Give your otherworldly hideout a little extra spark.
chisel.guide.energized_voidstone.title: Energized Voidstone
chisel.guide.factory.description: Dress your workshop like it means business. The lunch break is up to you.
chisel.guide.factory.title: Factory
chisel.guide.fantasy.description: Build a storybook setting in base, purple, green, blue or red. Every castle deserves an outfit.

chisel.guide.kitchen.title: Kitchen
chisel.guide.laboratory.description: A fresh, tidy home for your next brilliant experiment. Lab coat optional.
chisel.guide.laboratory.title: Laboratory
chisel.guide.lavastone.description: Give your walls a lava-inspired look and your fortress a dramatic welcome.
chisel.guide.lavastone.title: Lavastone
chisel.guide.lights.description: Give your favorite corner its moment in the spotlight, with colors to suit the mood.
chisel.guide.limestone.description: Lovely limestone for a little courtyard, a grand facade or whatever you're dreaming up.
chisel.guide.limestone.title: Limestone
chisel.guide.limestone.usage: Grab a Chisel and give limestone a new look. Try a few variants beside your doorway; a little stone shopping can change the whole entrance.
chisel.guide.liminal.description: That hallway looks familiar... Build your own backrooms and remember where you put the exit.
chisel.guide.liminal.title: Liminal
chisel.guide.marble.description: Treat your floor, foyer or favorite monument to a little marble elegance.
chisel.guide.marble.title: Marble
chisel.guide.marble.usage: Use a Chisel to browse marble's decorative variants. Try one as a floor, a column or a bit of trim. Even a tiny foyer can feel rather grand.
chisel.guide.measuring_tape.description: Settle the age-old question: will that roof actually fit?
chisel.guide.measuring_tape.details: Both endpoints count, and the measurement follows the largest difference along any axis. Once you've measured a span, your next click starts a new one.
chisel.guide.measuring_tape.tip: Sneak and right click to start again at that block. For a straight span, line both endpoints up on one axis. Measure twice, rebuild less!
chisel.guide.measuring_tape.title: Measuring Tape
chisel.guide.measuring_tape.usage: Right click a block with the Measuring Tape to mark your starting point. Right click another block and check chat for the distance. Much easier than counting windows and losing your place.
chisel.guide.military.description: Kit out a sturdy base, then give the lookout somewhere nice to stand.
chisel.guide.military.title: Military
chisel.guide.mossy_temple.description: Let the greenery move in. These ruins have had plenty of time to get cozy.
chisel.guide.mossy_temple.title: Mossy Temple
chisel.guide.nexus.description: Give your next futuristic base the kind of walls a spaceship would envy.
chisel.guide.nexus.title: Nexus
chisel.guide.offset_tool.description: Nudge a big pattern until it sits just right. A little wand magic!
chisel.guide.offset_tool.details: The wand shifts textures across the chunk, so step back and check the whole pattern after a nudge.
chisel.guide.offset_tool.tip: Follow the highlighted direction to line things up. Your blocks stay put while their textures do the shuffling.
chisel.guide.offset_tool.title: Ender Offset Wand
chisel.guide.offset_tool.usage: Right click a supported Chisel block with the Ender Offset Wand. A triangular overlay shows where you can shift its multiblock texture.
chisel.guide.palette_builder.description: A paint box for your blocks. Stir up a mix, try it on a wall and save your favorite recipe!
chisel.guide.palette_builder.details: Shop for blocks on the left: search by name or use the color filters, then click a block to add it. On the right, adjust each entry's weight or switch it Off to audition the mix without removing it.
chisel.guide.palette_builder.preview: Take your wall for a spin: drag to rotate, Shift-drag to move, scroll to zoom and double-click to reset. Click Shuffle for another arrangement. Like the ingredients but want the moss beside a doorway? Place that special detail by hand.
chisel.guide.palette_builder.screenshot: Your little mixing studio: block shopping on the left, a sample wall above your weighted ingredients on the right. This is the Weathered Castle starter mix, ready for a makeover.
chisel.guide.palette_builder.tip: Click Save when your mix makes you smile. Hold a Trowel, hold the Select Mode / Palette key, scroll to your saved palette and release. Bring the materials in survival; the palette remembers the recipe, and you supply the ingredients.
chisel.guide.palette_builder.title: Palette Brush
chisel.guide.palette_builder.usage: Right click with the Palette Brush to open your library. Pick New palette for a fresh start, or open a starter mix and give it your own twist. Name it something you'll recognize when it's time to build.
chisel.guide.palette_builder.weights: More weight means more chances to appear. A weight of 20 is twice as likely as 10; the numbers don't need to total 100. Try mostly stone bricks with a little cobblestone and a pinch of moss. The percentages help you see the balance.
chisel.guide.paperwall.description: Make a quiet corner, divide a room and give your tea table a lovely backdrop.
chisel.guide.paperwall.title: Paperwall
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.all_sid: Take a lap. Does the entrance face where people arrive? Does the back look finished? Drop a workbench and storage inside, then walk between them. If it feels cramped, move a wall now, before you've fallen in love with the flower boxes.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.check: Before decorating, take one more lap: an easy-to-find door, room to work, and a roof that looks good from the back as well as the front. Happy with all three? Time to pick some materials.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.compare: Same width, different amounts of elbow room. Both shells below are 7 blocks wide with three-block walls. The left is 5 blocks deep; the right is 9. The little one could make a nice kiosk. The longer one has room to spread out your workshop.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.descrip: A few rough walls now can save a lot of pickaxe work later.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.footpri: Here's the plan from above. Gray is the wall, cyan is your walking route, yellow is the workbench and orange is storage. The colors are just planning marks. Keep that cyan route clear and you can get to everything.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.goal: Let's give your workshop room for more than a crafting table and your elbows.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.practic: Grab some spare blocks and rough out your own workshop. Give it three-block walls, a two-block-high entrance and a temporary roof. Wander through it. Move things around until it feels useful; the fancy bits can wait.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.purpose: What goes inside? For our workshop: a crafting table, storage and space to walk between them. Mark a spot 7 blocks wide and 9 deep. With one-block walls, that leaves a 5 by 7 interior. A simple rectangle is a perfectly good start.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.silhoue: Pop a roof on the deeper shell and it starts looking like a building. This stepped gable sticks out one block past the walls. Try its height beside your neighbors, and leave yourself some headroom. A flat roof or a lower pitch could work here too.
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.title: Planning Your Build
chisel.guide.planning_your_build.transfe: Fancy a different look? Keep the workbench and storage, but try a flat-roofed studio or a sturdy little shed. See how the same space can feel like a whole new place. Up next: Understanding Block Palettes.
chisel.guide.road_lines.description: Point your town in the right direction with lanes, crossings and tidy intersections.
chisel.guide.road_lines.title: Road Lines
chisel.guide.shingles.description: Top off your cozy cottage or give that garden shed a roof worth admiring.
chisel.guide.shingles.title: Shingles
chisel.guide.smashing_rock.description: For when your stonework could use a little less perfection.
chisel.guide.smashing_rock.details: What happens depends on the block: stone bricks become cracked stone bricks, while stone can go through cobblestone, gravel and sand. Try a small sample to find the finish you like.
chisel.guide.smashing_rock.tip: Each throw uses one Smashing Rock. Give your sample a look between throws; that charming old wall may only need one good bonk.
chisel.guide.smashing_rock.title: Smashing Rock
chisel.guide.smashing_rock.usage: Right click to throw a Smashing Rock. On block impact, it transforms nearby supported blocks into their rougher or crushed counterparts. A very direct approach to weathering!
chisel.guide.steampunk.description: Gears, pipes and rusty plating for a workshop with wonderfully big ambitions.
chisel.guide.steampunk.title: Steampunk
chisel.guide.technical.description: Panels for the machine room you've been planning. Looking busy is part of the charm.
chisel.guide.technical.title: Technical
chisel.guide.temple.description: Build an ancient wonder, then decide which corner deserves the mysterious doorway.
chisel.guide.temple.title: Temple
chisel.guide.trowel.description: Give your walls a happy shuffle, one block at a time.
chisel.guide.trowel.details: For a saved mix, hold the Select Mode / Palette key, scroll to a palette and release to confirm. The Trowel picks available materials by weight from your inventory and offhand. Choose Hotbar the same way whenever you fancy a change.
chisel.guide.trowel.tip: Big wall, small pockets? Sneak and right click an accessible inventory to link extra materials for palette mode. Repeat on that inventory to unlink it. Hotbar mode draws only from your hotbar.
chisel.guide.trowel.title: Trowel
chisel.guide.trowel.usage: Right click a block face with the Trowel to place a material. In Hotbar mode, it picks randomly from eligible block slots in your hotbar. Load a few favorites and see what turns up!
chisel.guide.tyrian.description: Give your doorway a bold frame and your grand hall a little swagger.
chisel.guide.tyrian.title: Tyrian
chisel.guide.understanding_block_palette: Give it a glance from walking distance. You should still be able to spot the main surface and that special accent. If everything is shouting for attention, give one material a little more room.

These windows have the same shape and glass, but a different wardrobe. Left: oak walls, stone-brick base, spruce trim. Right: smooth quartz, polished deepslate and cyan. Which would you use for a cozy workshop? How about a bright modern studio?

Light and dark help parts stand apart. Spruce outlines pale oak, and deepslate gives bright quartz a strong base. If your frame disappears into the wall, try a lighter or darker block before making the frame bigger.

Some textures are busy; others give your eyes a rest. Cobblestone brings lots of little edges, while smoother blocks make quieter patches. Stand back to see how they mix. You don't need a magic number of blocks or a perfect percentage.
Find a handful of blocks that look happy living next to each other.
That block you love in your hotbar? Let's find out whether it gets along with the wall.
Color sets the mood. Warm wood and cool cyan take a build in different directions. Put a few blocks together at your actual building site; inventory icons don't tell the whole story.
Make a little wall with a main material, a base and a bit of trim. Swap just the base, then step back. Better? Worse? Weirdly perfect? Keep the version you like.

Give your materials a job. Your primary block covers the main surface. Supporting blocks might make the base or roof. An accent picks out something special, like a doorway. A rare little detail can be lovely too; it doesn't have to turn up on every wall.
A block's job and its random weight are different things. A high weight makes a tool pick it more often. It won't know that you wanted all those accents around the front door.
Take your wooden workshop's palette shopping for a modern studio: a pale wall, a dark base and a splash of color. Same jobs, different blocks. Up next: Adding Shape and Depth.
A saved palette remembers the mix, but you'll still need to bring the blocks. Chisel Tools: Palette Brush and Trowel covers saving and using it.

Here's one mix to play with. Weights are relative: 20 has twice the selection weight of 10, and they don't need to add up to 100. They choose how often a block comes up, so place important repairs and accents yourself.
chisel.guide.using_texture_intentionally: If you can still spot the patch or fade from walking distance, it's doing its job. If the wall just looks busy, simplify a little and take another look.

Here's the same wall three ways: clean bricks, scattered cobblestone, then a grouped patch. The last two both use six cobblestone blocks and nineteen stone bricks. Same ingredients, different arrangement. Which one looks like somebody came back to patch a hole?
Give your walls a little history, or just a really good pattern.
A handful of different blocks can look like an old repair, a smooth fade or a very confused wall. Placement makes the difference.

Want a fade instead? This sample climbs from dark deepslate to lighter stone over five rows. The texture changes along with the color. Try a small strip first, and add gentler steps or different blocks if the jump feels too sudden.

On the right, those six cobblestone blocks gather into a two-by-three patch at the lower left. The close-up below shows it clearly. The scattered version could suit a rough old wall too; it depends on the story you want to tell.

Shuffle nineteen stone bricks and six cobblestone into a five-by-five wall. Now gather the cobblestone into a patch, filling the old spots with bricks. Back up a few steps. Give the patch a new shape if it isn't reading how you hoped.

Maybe the base is damp. Maybe a corner got repaired. Maybe the owner keeps meaning to fix that panel. You're suggesting a history with blocks, rather than simulating real weathering. One small patch can do plenty of storytelling.
Keep a studio spotless with one neat band, or give a shed a few replacement panels by the service door. Both can have character. Up next: Details and Lighting.

Mixing surfaces adds variation. Moving from one color or lightness to another makes a gradient. A patch of worn or mossy blocks can suggest age. Pick the look you're after, then let the arrangement help it along.
chisel.guide.valentines.description: Build a sweetheart cottage or add a playful touch to a room you love.
chisel.guide.valentines.title: Valentine's
chisel.guide.voidstone.description: A little mystery for your walls. What lives in that tower is entirely up to you.
chisel.guide.voidstone.title: Voidstone
chisel.guide.warning_signs.description: Give your questionable experiments a proper warning sign. Very professional.
chisel.guide.warning_signs.title: Warning Signs
chisel.guide.waterstone.description: Bring a water-inspired pattern to a bathhouse, fountain surround or seaside retreat.
chisel.guide.waterstone.title: Waterstone
chisel.guide.your_first_build.adapt: Here's one way it could turn out. Yours might have a different palette, a door around the side or a spotless finish. Swap the workshop interior for cottage furniture if you'd rather live here. Make room for whatever you'll actually do inside.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.brief: We'll start with the shape, pick some materials, play with depth, then add texture and finishing touches. Keep a crafting table, storage and a clear way in. The examples are here to borrow from; your workshop can take its own turns.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.check: Take the grand tour: find the door, walk around inside, admire the back and come by after sunset. If it feels good to use and looks like a place you meant to build, call it home.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.depth: Give a window some depth. On a separate five-by-five wall, leave a one-wide, two-high opening. Move the glass one block behind the wall, then add a ring of trim one block in front. The close-up below shows how it fits together. Borrow the idea wherever it suits your workshop.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.descriptio: Let's turn that pile of blocks into a place you'd actually use.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.details: Put a roof over it. The example uses a stepped gable with a one-block overhang. Take a lap to see it from every side. Add your workbench, storage and a lantern by the approach, keeping the route clear. Visit after dark too; the preview can't show you the real lighting.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.fade: Your turn to improvise: give another window or the doorway a look you like. Flat, recessed or framed all work. Keep the materials the same while you try the shapes, and take a peek from the side before choosing.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.goal: One little workshop, plenty of room to make it yours.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.palette: Pick an outfit. Oak walls, a stone-brick base and spruce roof or trim make a cozy start. For a modern look, try smooth quartz, polished deepslate and cyan. Put a few blocks together first and see which combination you want to come home to.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.practice: Put the last few blocks on your workshop, then see what else the idea can become. A tiny studio? A garden shed? Keep a detail you love and change the rest to fit its new job.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.shape: Start with the walls. Mark a 7 by 9 footprint and build three blocks high. Leave a centered doorway one block wide and two tall. You'll have a 5 by 7 interior. Leave side windows and try walking between a workbench and storage. The open shell below gives you a peek inside.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.texture: Newly built or a little lived-in? Keep the walls clean, or add a small repair. Our workshop has two replacement wood panels on one side. Step back to see whether yours adds character or steals the show from the entrance.
chisel.guide.your_first_build.title: Your First Build
chisel.guide.your_first_build.transfer: Got another idea already? Start with a rough shape and follow it. The other guides are here whenever you want to try a new palette, window or finishing touch. There's always room for one more build.
